name: @thetis/gh
description: The GitHub CLI as tools, run as a bot user with a token and no ssh key: one gh command at a time, resolved by gh itself and checked against a fixed denylist and your own allow, deny and read-only settings, the REST and GraphQL API, git over https as the bot, gh's help, and what gh is signed in as.

toolGroup.brief: Work with GitHub through the gh CLI as a bot user: repositories, pull requests, issues, reviews, Actions runs and workflows, releases, gists, the REST and GraphQL API, and git clone/fetch/push over https.

tools.name: gh_run
tools.description: Run one gh (GitHub CLI) command as the bot user and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. Give the words after `gh` as `args` (preferred) or one `command` line; they are passed as arguments, never to a shell, so pipes and `&&` do not work: run one command per call and shape output with gh's own --json, --jq, --template and --limit. gh resolves the command first; an unknown command or flag is refused without running. Always refused: auth login/logout/token, codespace, extension, alias set, browse, completion, run watch, and --show-token. Your allow/deny/read-only settings apply on top. Text a command reads from stdin (a PR body with --body-file -, a JSON body with --input -) goes in `input`. This can create, change and delete things on GitHub: say what a mutating command will do before running it. Tips: pass --repo owner/repo when not in a checkout; use --json fields --jq expr to keep output small; give `cwd` for commands that act on a local checkout (pr create, pr checkout, repo clone).

args.description: The command as a list of words after `gh`, e.g. ["pr", "list", "--repo", "owner/repo", "--state", "open", "--json", "number,title,author"]. A value with spaces is one element.

command.description: The same as one line, split like a shell would split words (quotes honoured, nothing expanded). Use when args is awkward.

input.description: Text fed to the command's stdin, for `--body-file -`, `--input -`, `--notes-file -` and the like.

cwd.description: Directory to run in, relative to home: for commands that read a local git checkout (pr create, pr checkout, repo clone, run download).

dry_run.description: Only resolve the command and check it against the policy; run nothing.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait, 5-600. Defaults to the package's timeoutMs (120s).

tools.name: gh_api
tools.description: Call the GitHub REST or GraphQL API as the bot user through `gh api`. REST: `endpoint` like repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues (gh fills {owner} and {repo} from the checkout in cwd only; give them literally otherwise), `method` (default GET, or POST when params/body are given), `params` (flat fields, sent as JSON body or as query for GET) or `body` (a whole JSON body). GraphQL: `graphql` (the query or mutation) and `variables`. `paginate` fetches every page (REST pages are slurped into one array); `jq` filters the result; `headers` adds request headers such as Accept for previews. GET is read-only; anything else changes GitHub, so say what it will do first. Prefer gh_run when a gh subcommand exists for the job.

endpoint.description: REST path, e.g. repos/owner/repo/pulls/12/reviews or user/repos. A full https://api.github.com/ URL also works.

method.description: GET, POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE. Default GET, or POST when params or body are given.

params.description: Flat fields: strings are sent as strings, numbers/booleans/null typed (gh api -f/-F). Query parameters for GET, JSON body otherwise.

body.description: A whole JSON body (an object, or a JSON string), for nested payloads. Not with params.

graphql.description: A GraphQL query or mutation. Sets endpoint to graphql.

previews.description: API preview names to opt into (gh api -p).

jq.description: A jq expression applied to the response, e.g. .[].name or .data.repository.issues.nodes.

paginate.description: Fetch every page of a paginated list.

include.description: Include the response status line and headers in the output.

dry_run.description: Show the gh api command it would run, and run nothing.

tools.name: gh_git
tools.description: Run one git command with the bot's GitHub credentials (https only; this space has no ssh key), for clone, fetch, pull, push, checkout, branch, commit, status, log and diff on a checkout under home. Give the words after `git` as `args` or one `command` line, and `cwd` (the checkout, relative to home) for anything but clone. Remotes must be https://github.com/owner/repo.git; the token is supplied through gh's credential helper and never appears in the command or the remote URL. Commits are authored as the configured bot identity. `push` and `remote` are refused in read-only mode.

cwd.description: The checkout to run in, relative to home.

input.description: Text fed to git's stdin (e.g. a commit message with `commit -F -`, or a patch for `apply -`).

tools.name: gh_help
tools.description: Read gh's help for a command (usage, flags, examples), e.g. `pr create` or `api`. Use it before gh_run when unsure of a flag, instead of guessing.

args.description: The command path without flags, e.g. ["pr", "create"].

command.description: The command path as one line, e.g. "issue list".

full.description: Return up to 18000 characters instead of 9000.

tools.name: gh_status
tools.description: Show what gh_run runs as: the gh version, whether a bot token is configured and which account and scopes GitHub reports for it, the git identity commits will carry, and the allow/deny/read-only policy in force. Call it first, and whenever a command fails on auth.

token.help: The bot user's GitHub token (a fine-grained or classic personal access token, or a GitHub App installation token). Passed to gh and git as GH_TOKEN for each call; never written to disk or shown. Give the bot only the repositories and permissions the work needs.

host.help: GitHub host when not github.com (GH_HOST), e.g. github.example.com for GitHub Enterprise Server.

gitUserName.help: The name commits made through gh_git carry (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME / GIT_COMMITTER_NAME), e.g. the bot's display name.

gitUserEmail.help: The email commits made through gh_git carry, e.g. the bot's noreply address: <id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com.

mode.help: `full` (default) or `read-only`. read-only admits only commands that read (list, view, status, diff, checks, search, GET API calls, …) and refuses git push; full admits anything the lists allow.

allow.help: If set, only these gh commands or groups run: a comma-separated list or a JSON array, e.g. `pr, issue, repo view, api`.

deny.help: gh commands or groups refused on top of the fixed denylist: a comma-separated list or a JSON array, e.g. `repo delete, secret, ssh-key, gpg-key`.

configDir.help: gh's config directory (GH_CONFIG_DIR). Defaults to ~/.config/gh in this space; the token does not live there.

ghPath.help: Full path to the gh executable when it is not on the PATH.

gitPath.help: Full path to the git executable when it is not on the PATH.

timeoutMs.help: Default per-command timeout in milliseconds, clamped to 5000-600000.
